exercise.name: Single-Arm Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
aliases: One arm DB extension on bench

reference.title: Dumbbell One Arm Triceps Extension (on bench)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the dumbbell lowers beside the head, exhale as you straighten the arm.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.4 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: More reps, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet planted. Hold one dumbbell straight up over the shoulder, palm facing in; rest the other hand on your stomach.
Keep the upper arm vertical and breathe in as you bend the elbow, lowering the dumbbell beside the head.
Dumbbell beside the head, elbow pointing at the ceiling, stretch in the back of the arm.
Breathe out and straighten the elbow.
Arm straight, squeeze, repeat; then switch arms.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging back and forth
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing at the same spot; only the forearms move.
Keep both shoulder blades on the bench; brace lightly.

mistakes.mistake: Lowering too fast toward the head
mistakes.fix: Lower under control beside the head; keep the dumbbell clear of the face.
Straighten the elbows without snapping them.

kinematics.norm: From straight to a little past 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Vertical over the shoulder and still (clinical opinion)
Dumbbell beside the head, clear of the head and bench (clinical opinion)
Rests on the stomach; some lifters steady the working upper arm with it instead (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020 (head, shoulders and hips on the bench)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #036212, Dumbbell One Arm Triceps Extension (on bench), video (movement reference)
Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)

Maeo and Kanehisa, triceps hypertrophy after 12 weeks of elbow extension training with the shoulder at 180 versus 0 degrees of flexion (Descente Sports Science vol 41; full paper: Maeo et al. 2023, Eur J Sport Sci 23(7):1240-1250, PubMed 35819335)

cautions: Lower the dumbbell beside the head, never toward the face; use a fixed-plate dumbbell.
Elbow pain: shorten the range and use a lighter dumbbell (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: let the upper arm tilt slightly toward the head.
Elbow discomfort: lighter dumbbell, shorter range.
regressions: Two-arm skull crusher with light dumbbells.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Only mover: straightens the elbow while the upper arm stays vertical. Long and lateral head activity differed in lying barbell triceps extensions (Boehler 2011); the long head works at a longer length the higher the arm is raised (Maeo and Kanehisa).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm vertical as the dumbbell lowers behind the elbow.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still on the bench.

guides.label: Forearm swings back, upper arm still
Elbow a little past 90 at the bottom
